subject.title: feat(hooks): add agent turn end hook

question: Should OpenClaw support a stable ACP-only `agent:turn:end` internal-hook contract, or should turn completion remain on the existing plugin lifecycle path until the broader lifecycle-hook design is decided?
rationale: The branch adds a documented, public-facing lifecycle contract rather than repairing established behavior; code review cannot decide its desired scope, naming, timing, or relationship to existing `agent_end` plugin hooks.

options.title: Decide the lifecycle contract first
options.body: Use the broader lifecycle issue to accept, narrow, or reject the ACP-only event, then invite a fresh focused implementation PR.

options.title: Adopt the ACP-only contract
options.body: Explicitly sponsor the event name, payload, timing, and non-durable semantics, then request a clean replacement PR with current-head live proof.

options.title: Keep existing lifecycle hooks
options.body: Decline a parallel internal-hook contract and direct integrations to the existing plugin lifecycle surface where it is sufficient.

recommendation.title: Decide the lifecycle contract first
recommendation.body: Use the broader lifecycle issue to accept, narrow, or reject the ACP-only event, then invite a fresh focused implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ownership spans both the ACP manager lifecycle and the adjacent hook documentation contract.
